title: feat(layout,app-shell,console): the menu hides a `doc` entry the member may not read, and the docs portal refuses a direct route outside the audience (objectui#10188)
body:
Part of #10188: the menu half, as defence in depth, and (round 2, `230d6abb09`) the direct route. The seat answered the round-1 questions in-seat (`5918144377`): Q1 = B, a refusal distinct from "not found"; Q2 = A, a doc opens in the book that claims it. Both are in this PR. The platform-checklist item is drafted in the round-2 dev report (`5918851992`) for the seat to route to objectstack, which is why this stays `Part of`.
Clause-②: yes

Implemented by the `os-dev` run for claim `5916997645` (session `https://claude.ai/code/session_0122Knsowci76D2rBWReCzzZ`), branch `claude/issue-10188-doc-menu-audience`.

## Measured first: the server already hides the entry

I ran a probe backend on the **published** `@objectstack/cli` / `@objectstack/rest` **17.5.0**, the version objectui resolves. It serves one package with three books and two docs:

- `menuprobe_manual`: `org`, claims `menuprobe_gs_welcome`.
- `menuprobe_staff_manual`: `audience: { permissionSet: 'menuprobe_staff' }`, claims `menuprobe_staff_secret`.
- `menuprobe_empty_manual`: claims nothing.

The app `menuprobe_app` has one `doc` entry of every shape. There are three signed-in personas. The insider holds `menuprobe_staff`. The outsider and the seeded admin do not.

| read (outsider; the admin reads the same) | status |
|:--|:--|
| `GET /meta/app` and `GET /meta/app/menuprobe_app` | 200, and the navigation holds only `nav_open_doc`, `nav_open_book` and the url control. Every staff entry is gone, and the empty book's entry is gone for **every** persona |
| `GET /meta/doc` and `GET /meta/book` (lists) | 200, pruned per member: no `menuprobe_staff_secret`, no `menuprobe_staff_manual` |
| `GET /meta/doc/menuprobe_staff_secret` | **403** `PERMISSION_DENIED` "This documentation is limited to holders of a permission set you do not have" (anonymous: 401 `UNAUTHENTICATED`) |
| `GET /meta/doc/menuprobe_no_such_doc` (control) | **404** `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` |
| `GET /meta/book/menuprobe_staff_manual` and its `/tree` | 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED` |

The insider's reads carry every staff entry, doc and book. `objectstack` commit `bc80e16260` (objectstack#19790, "app nav prunes doc entries the caller may not read") is an ancestor of the `@objectstack/rest@17.5.0` tag (`merge-base --is-ancestor` exit 0). The console, driven in Chromium on this branch against that backend, draws the same: the outsider's menu is `Open doc · Open book · Control url`, and the insider's adds the three staff entries.

So the dispatch's mechanism assumption 2 (a `doc` entry renders for every member) is **falsified in the real shell**. The member never receives the entry.

## What this PR adds: the renderer's pruning, as defence in depth (round 1), and the direct route (round 2)

The ruling on objectstack#19790 (letter A, maintainer batch #217) keeps the renderer's pruning. Its point 2: "The renderer's pruning (objectstack-ai/objectui#10188) stays — the server is the authority, the renderer is defence in depth." This PR is that pruning. It hides what the member's own reads omit and re-derives no audience in the browser.

**`@object-ui/layout`**
- `checkDocTarget?: DocTargetChecker` is a new optional guard on `NavigationRenderer`, `AppSchemaRenderer` and `hasVisibleNavigationItems` (`NavigationVisibilityOptions`). It is asked `{ book, doc }` for a `type: 'doc'` entry, and `false` hides the entry.
- The guard joins the one shared guard statement (`passesNavItemGuards`). Sidebar rows, the derived area visibility and the Favorites section therefore read it alike. Without it, `doc` entries draw exactly as before.
- `DocNavTarget` and `DocTargetChecker` are exported.

**`@object-ui/app-shell`**
- `useNavDocTargetCheck` (new, internal) answers the guard from the member's `doc` / `book` lists. They are read through `MetadataProvider`'s per-type cache, the shell's one metadata door, once per type and only when the navigation holds a `doc` entry.
  - A page is readable when the member's `doc` list names it.
  - A book is readable when the member's `book` list names it, or when its name is the package of a doc the member reads (the implicit per-package book).
  - A page in a book needs both.
- While a list is loading or failed, or outside a provider, the hook answers nothing and the server's app stands.
- Wired into `UnifiedSidebar` (the app navigation and the area derivation) and into `nav:menu` (its guards and its own copy of the guard sequence).

**Docs.** The `doc` bullet of `content/docs/guide/designing-app-navigation.md` now says the author does not repeat the audience on the entry: a member who may not read what it opens does not see it.

**Round 2, `@object-ui/console` (the direct route).**
- `DocPage` reads the client's declared `httpStatus`: 401 / 403 render `DocRefusal` ("You do not have access to this documentation" with the server's reason), in place of "Failed to load documentation".
- `DocsSlug` asks the server once, by name (the doc, then the book), about a segment none of the member's lists answers. 401 / 403 render the refusal. A 404, or a name nothing carries, still renders "Documentation not found".
- `homeBook` (`book-nav.ts`) prefers, among the doc's own package's books, the one that claims it, else that package's first book. So a `{doc}` entry opens in its book's context. `scopeDocsToBook` is untouched (objectui#11245).
- `DocRefusal` is exported from `BookPage.tsx`.

**Changesets.** One per released package: `@object-ui/layout` minor, `@object-ui/app-shell` minor, `@object-ui/console` minor (round 2).

### Why this shape (Zone 2 item 3, measured)

- **Not `checkCapability`.** Widening `CapabilityChecker`'s `kind` union to `'doc' | 'book'` breaks every explicitly typed host checker. `UnifiedSidebar` and `nav:menu` declare theirs as taking `'object' | 'service'`. A strict `tsc` probe of exactly that assignment answers TS2322: `Type '"doc"' is not assignable to type '"object" | "service"'`. The two checkers also ask different questions. Capability asks whether the RUNTIME has the target (fails open). This one asks whether the MEMBER may read it. The server keeps the same split: its docs gate is separate from its service and servability gates.
- **One guard pipeline.** The new check sits inside `passesNavItemGuards`, not beside it.
- **The data: why the portal's shared fetch is not the source.** `BookDataProvider` lives in the console app, under the `/docs` routes. The menu hosts (`UnifiedSidebar`, `nav:menu`) live in the published `@object-ui/app-shell`, above those routes, and cannot import the app's context. Re-pointing the portal at the shell cache would change the portal's freshness and its preview-mode world, which is outside this card. The hook adds no fetching code of its own; it reads the shell's existing per-type cache.
- **Book membership is not re-derived.** A doc's effective audience is the union over every book that claims it. So a book whose own audience admits the member admits every page it claims, and list membership answers the book's whole audience question.
  - Whether an admitted book claims any page at all is a content question, the same for every member. The server's nav gate answers it: the empty book above is pruned server-side for everyone.
  - The member's `doc` list carries only `name`, `label` and `_packageId`, not the placement keys, so the browser could not re-derive membership anyway.
- **No spec runtime import in the eager sidebar.** `@objectstack/spec/system`'s resolver would have answered the empty-book case. Today it is imported only by lazily loaded views, and it would enter the sidebar's eager closure unmeasured (`check:eager-closure` needs a full console build). So it is not used.

## Pins, reds and ablations

- `packages/layout/src/__tests__/NavigationRenderer.docAudience-10188.test.tsx` (8 tests):
  - three checker-driven cases: readable, unreadable (page, book, page-in-book) and empty book;
  - the exact target asked;
  - Favorites;
  - the derived area visibility;
  - `AppSchemaRenderer` forwarding;
  - the no-checker control.
  - **Red before the fix:** 6 failed and 2 passed (the readable case and the no-checker control).
- `packages/app-shell/src/layout/__tests__/UnifiedSidebar.docAudience-10188.test.tsx` (5 tests): the real sidebar over the **real** `MetadataProvider`, fed by an adapter that answers per member. The app document still carries every entry, as a server that did not prune would send it.
  - outsider vs insider;
  - the implicit package book;
  - the lists read once per type;
  - no list read for an app with no `doc` entry;
  - no `book` read for a page-only menu.
- `packages/app-shell/src/views/__tests__/nav-doc-audience-10188.render.test.tsx` (2 tests): the sidebar and `nav:menu` agree, and nothing is hidden while the lists load.

Every ablation went through objectstack's `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` in wrap mode (the anchor must hit, the blob moved, the restore proven as blob == HEAD with `git diff HEAD` empty), with the three pin files run each time. `@object-ui/layout` resolves to source through the root vitest alias, so no dist rebuild was involved.

| leg | mutation | red |
|:--|:--|:--|
| A1 | the guard line in `passesNavItemGuards` deleted | 10 of 15 |
| A2 | `checkDocTarget` not handed to the sidebar's `NavigationRenderer` | 3 of 15 (the outsider cases) |
| A3 | `nav:menu`'s own guard line deleted | 1 of 15 (its surface in the agreement pin) |
| A4 | the implicit-book half of the book rule dropped | first attempt **refused by the tool, nothing ran**: the replacement text also occurred inside the anchor. Redone with a distinct replacement: 1 of 15 (the outsider's package-book entry) |
| A5 | the loading guard dropped | 1 of 15 (nothing hidden while loading) |

- **Live, in Chromium, on this branch against the 17.5.0 backend:**
  - The outsider's `/meta/app` response was intercepted to put every entry back, as a non-pruning server would send it. The outsider's menu is still `Open doc · Open book · Control url`.
  - With A2 held on disk, the same run draws all three staff entries.
  - Each list is requested once, and there are no page errors.
- **Cross-package reverse check.** Renaming the prop to `checkDocTargetX` in `UnifiedSidebar` turns `app-shell`'s `tsc --noEmit` red (TS2322 against `NavigationRendererProps`), and it was restored. This proves app-shell reads the rebuilt `packages/layout/dist/NavigationRenderer.d.ts`, which is in its test program.

## Gates

**Round 2, at head `230d6abb09`**, exit captured before any pipe:
- Build: `turbo run build --filter='@object-ui/console^...'`: 34 of 34 tasks, exit 0. `pnpm --filter @object-ui/console type-check`: exit 0. The console's own `tsc` was missing from round 1's local union; that is how round 2's first head reached CI red, and it was fixed by narrowing in `230d6abb09`.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/console build` then `pnpm check:eager-closure`: exit 0. Eager closure 3581.6 KB of 3607.4 KB (headroom 25.9 KB). `DocsLayout`, `DocsSlug`, `DocPage` and `BookPage` are lazy.
- `vitest run apps/console/` (the whole console project): 135 files, 1572 tests passed. The new pin `apps/console/src/pages/docs-portal.directRoute-10188.test.tsx` (11 tests) was red first at `e503eaaa8f` (7 failed | 4 passed).
- Ablations B1–B4, each red as predicted and each restored clean: the `DocPage` refusal branch (2 of 49 red), the `DocsSlug` refusal render (4 of 49), the book half of the probe (2 of 49), and `homeBook`'s claiming preference (1 of 49).
- CI on `230d6abb09`: 43 check-runs, 40 success, 3 skipped, 0 failure.

**Round 1, at head `e503eaaa8f`**, exit captured before any pipe:

- Build: `pnpm --workspace-concurrency=2 --filter '@object-ui/app-shell^...' build` (29 of 47 projects, layout included): exit 0.
- Type-check: `pnpm --filter @object-ui/layout type-check` and `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check` (both `tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`): exit 0. `--listFiles` shows every new test file in its package's test program.
- Tests: `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=3` over 155 files, exit 0, 1490 tests passed. The files are:
  - `packages/layout/` (the whole package);
  - 73 app-shell test files that mount `UnifiedSidebar`, `ConsoleLayout`, `nav:menu`, `NavigationRenderer`, `AppContent` or `ConsoleShell`;
  - the four `packages/types` pins that name `NavigationRenderer`;
  - `apps/console/src/pages/*.test.*`;
  - `AppPreview.docEntry-11197`.
- Repo checks, each exit 0:
  - `check:docs-route-closure`, `check:phantom-deps`, `check:new-line-citations` (0 new), `check:control-bytes`;
  - `check:doc-fences`, `docs:check-links`, `markdown-test-inputs --audit`;
  - `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:vi-mock-inherit`, `check:vi-mock-override-shape`, `check:test-path-roots`;
  - `check:unused-deps`, `check:unreferenced-sources`, `check:doc-types`;
  - `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check-changeset-presence` (round 1: 8 source files of 2 released packages, 2 changesets; at round 2's head, 13 source files of 3 released packages, 3 changesets), `check-changeset-no-major`.
- `check:changeset-claims` names two pending changesets that describe an edited file (`6335-starred-apps-nav-exclusion`, `8871-page-node-refuses-breadcrumbs`). Both paragraphs were re-read, and neither is falsified. The pending `11197-doc-nav-entry` also stays true: a `doc` entry is still gated by its siblings' base keys and the audience gate stays the server's. The new checker answers from the server's own lists.
- ESLint, round 1, narrowed to its 8 changed `.ts` / `.tsx` files (`--format json`): 0 errors. Round 2 ran the same check on its 5 files, each against its round-2 base, with the same result: 0 errors and no new warnings.
  - The four modified files carry exactly their base's warnings, 10 / 11 / 2 / 25, each read with `git show BASE:path | eslint --stdin`. The four new files carry 0.
  - The population is each package's `lint` script, `eslint .`. There is no type-aware `parserOptions` and no local rule reads the filesystem, so no untouched file's verdict can move.
- Governed surface: `check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` says NOT GOVERNED for all 11 of round 1's paths, and for all 17 files at round 2's head.
- Round 1 did not measure `check:eager-closure`; round 2 measured it (above). The full app-shell suite beyond the 73 files is CI's, and CI is green.

## The direct route (round 2): a refusal, not "not found"

Measured live on a published `@objectstack/cli` 17.5.0 backend, as the outsider. `/docs/DOC`, `/docs/BOOK`, `/docs/BOOK/DOC` and the same three under `/apps/PKG/docs` each render "You do not have access to this documentation", with the server's reason, in place. Round 1 showed "Documentation not found … is installed" or "Failed to load documentation" there. A name nothing carries still renders "Documentation not found". The reader lands in the claiming book: `/docs/menuprobe_gs_welcome` goes to `menuprobe_manual`, where round 1 sent it to `menuprobe_empty_manual`.

## Acceptance notes (not filed)

- ~~A flat `doc` permalink opens in the wrong book's context when a package ships several books.~~ Fixed in round 2 (`homeBook` prefers the claiming book; see above).
- `AppSchemaRenderer`'s mobile bottom nav applies no item guard at all: not `visible`, not permissions, not capabilities, and so not this one. The console does not mount `AppSchemaRenderer`. This predates the card.
- A book the server prunes for having no claimed page (the empty book) still opens a page from its package's Uncategorized group on its direct URL. The menu entry is gone, so only a typed URL reaches it.
- The seeded admin does not hold `menuprobe_staff` and is refused like the outsider. That is the server's audience rule as written, and noted only.
